Report the deletion count, restored comments, reruns, architect sketch, fixes, encoding offers, encodings, unenforced constraints, and other open work.\\n\\n## Capability and permission limits\\n\\nThe Comment Sicko role edits only scoped comments when writes are authorized and available. Its final response is a report; that format does not prohibit its comment edits. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Prove It Works\\n\\nVerify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or \\\"it compiles.\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.\\n\\nCheck the real thing, not a proxy:\\n- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state\\n- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation\\n- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system\\n\\n## Script the check when you can\\n\\nThe strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.\\n\\nKeep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n\\n\"\n    }\n  },\n  {\n    \"tool\": \"exec_command\",\n    \"args\": {\n      \"cmd\": \"bun -e 'const t=await Bun.file(\\\"task-contract.json\\\").json(); for(const p of t.sourceFiles.slice(11,14)){console.log(\\\"FILE \\\"+p+\\\"\\\\n\\\"+await Bun.file(p).text())}'\",\n      \"workdir\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/fixtures/cases/stack-resume\",\n      \"max_output_tokens\": 16000\n    },\n    \"result\": {\n      \"chunk_id\": \"becfb5\",\n      \"wall_time_seconds\": 0.000006083,\n      \"exit_code\": 0,\n      \"original_token_count\": 2711,\n      \"output\": \"FILE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path. These documents live at the package root. Prepare a reviewable title, body, verification artifacts, and intended base before any external operation. Record explicit authorization, the repository, branch head, destination and action identity. Check the destination after an interrupted action before any replay. Missing access or permission leaves the external action blocked and the content available locally. Draft-only permission permits a draft, never readiness, push, merge or comments.\\n\\n**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple independent workers on the same branch each get their own isolated worktree. Preserve unrelated dirty work before creating an authorized fresh worktree. Report a snarled worktree instead of resetting or discarding unowned changes. Missing independent workers permits an authorized sequential reduction, never a claim of independent review.\\n\\n**Commits.** Commit liberally within the authorized local scope. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.\\n\\n**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit if that external skill is exposed and authorized. It is not bundled here. Run `/no-comments` through [no-comments](../../no-comments/SKILL.md) before review. Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.\\n\\n**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.\\n\\nPut each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.\\n\\n- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a \\\"based on main\\\" preamble.\\n- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.\\n- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.\\n- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.\\n- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.\\n- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.\\n\\nAfter these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or \\\"CLEAN\\\" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.\\n\\n**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).\\n\\n**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its exposed instructions define the actual interface. An unavailable, denied or failed tool is a stated blocker, not permission to bypass its tracking through a CLI. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.\\n\\n**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.\\n\\n**Readiness.** The source workflow opens every PR ready, never as a draft, when readiness is explicitly authorized. If only draft creation is authorized, preserve that limit and create a draft through the exposed tool or `gh pr create --draft`. Verify the actual draft state and report the readiness gate open. Use Origin draft creation only when its current interface supports it. Otherwise report blocked. All readiness instructions below require readiness authorization. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so use its observed ready-creation interface, such as `draft: false` only when that field is actually supported. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Run `origin pr view <number>` or `gh pr view <number>` before you refer to PR status.\\n\\n**Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run a separate babysit pass only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists. A babysit for each new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits that later waves restart. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.\\n\\nA subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate` through [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md), `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask [babysit](babysit.md) waits for. The owner starts the loop after its code-ready report and reports merge-ready or STACK-READY as its playbook says. The rules here and in [babysit](babysit.md) that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.\\n\\nFor the owner exception, read [Autopilot-full](autopilot-full.md) or [Autopilot-stack](autopilot-stack.md) and the [Bugbot triage rubric](../references/bugbot-triage.md). These briefs assign babysitting only within explicit user authorization and observed capabilities. Opening a PR alone never supplies that authorization. No watcher, bootstrap or orchestration helper runs in this opening step. Babysit owns the actual watcher binding.\\n\\n\"\n    }\n  },\n  {\n    \"tool\": \"exec_command\",\n    \"args\": {\n      \"cmd\": \"cat README.md committed-inputs/shared/README.md committed-inputs/shared/forge.json; bun -e 'const t=await Bun.file(\\\"task-contract.json\\\").json(); console.log(await Bun.file(t.sourceFiles[5]).text())'\",\n      \"workdir\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/fixtures/cases/stack-resume\",\n      \"max_output_tokens\": 11000\n    },\n    \"result\": {\n      \"chunk_id\": \"f4a1b0\",\n      \"wall_time_seconds\": 0.000005584,\n      \"exit_code\": 0,\n      \"original_token_count\": 8552,\n      \"output\": \"# Synthetic task inputs\\nThis repository identifies inert workflow inputs and current case contracts. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\nmode: true\\nicon: crown\\ncolor: yellow\\nreminder: New task? Playbook match or rigor needed -> apply /poteto-mode. Casual turn or user opts out -> don't.\\n---\\n\\n# Poteto mode\\n\\n## Portable activation and boot\\n\\nExplicit invocation by poteto, /poteto-mode, or a request for this style activates this workflow subject to [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Retain the active controller for unqualified follow-ups. Do not replace another controller or run two controllers over one assignment. If both are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before dispatch or writes.\\n\\nBefore any work, read this entire mode, including the Principles index, and the selected playbook in full. Read each applied principle leaf in full this session. A summary does not satisfy these reads. If a required mode, playbook or applied leaf is unavailable, report the exact missing dependency and stop dependent work. Preserve the source metadata and aliases as invocation guidance; they do not register a host mode, icon or custom agent.\\n\\nDiscover operations using [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Follow [assignment and integration](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Observed bindings and user permissions govern execution. Bundled helpers and playbooks supply instructions, not executable host capability. Never install or configure a companion implicitly.\\n\\n## Non-negotiables\\n\\nThe Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.\\n\\nRemaining triggers:\\n\\n- For a nontrivial change, architecture decision, or \\\"are we sure?\\\", use the **how** skill.\\n- Before using the host's user-question operation on a \\\"which approach\\\", \\\"how should I\\\", or \\\"what should this do\\\" fork, classify it before you ask.\\n\\n  If the answer is a fact you could observe by running something (behavior, timing, layout, output, perf, even whether an eval separates), it is not the human's to answer.\\n\\n  Sketch it via the Prototype playbook (`playbooks/prototype.md`) and let the result decide.\\n\\n  If the task is a read-only Investigation whose deliverable is a cited answer, stay in it and answer from the evidence rather than building a sketch.\\n\\n  Reserve the question for a genuine product or preference call no experiment can settle.\\n\\n  Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call that the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer.\\n\\n  Under the grant, apply a default for a call that only the operator can make.\\n\\n  Report the default with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead.\\n\\n  The operator answers in their own words.\\n\\n  Never give a shorthand token to type back.\\n\\n  Gates that the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.\\n- For any code, name the data shape first, and choose its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**.\\n- For code crossing a function boundary, use the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.\\n- For parallel fan-out, use the **swarm** skill for coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, and exploration partitions. Use **arena** for design or code bakeoffs with base selection and grafting.\\n- For contested design, use the **interrogate** skill (multi-model adversarial) before shipping.\\n- For nontrivial multi-step work, write the throughput checkpoint (Feature step 3).\\n- For any prose surface, use the **unslop** skill. Your reply is a prose surface. Write it per **Writing the reply**. Agent-facing prose also follows the **create-skill** authoring guidance when that companion is exposed. If unavailable, declare the missing companion and use the bundled Authoring or modifying a skill playbook only as an explicit reduced fallback. Do not claim the absent companion ran.\\n- For docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages, use the **technical-writing** skill (`/technical-writing`).\\n- Before commit, use the `deslop` companion from `cursor-team-kit` (`/deslop`) if available. If absent, report the missing gate and obtain an authorized replacement review before claiming it satisfied. Do not install it implicitly.\\n- Before review, use the **no-comments** companion (`/no-comments`) if available. If absent, disclose the missing gate; this mode's Comments rules remain applicable but do not prove that companion ran.\\n- When shipping UI / IDE / CLI, use the matching control skill. `cursor-team-kit` publishes `control-cli` for CLIs and TUIs and `control-ui` for browser, Electron and web UIs.\\n\\n  Discover their availability and the actual exposed control tools.\\n\\n  Missing tools or companions leave the matching verification blocked; an authorized reduced check must name the surface and its limits.\\n\\n  For bug fixes, reproduce first on the same surface yourself.\\n\\n  Hand to the user only under the narrow Bug fix step 1 exception.\\n- When running a benchmark, measuring perf yourself, or reporting a speedup or regression you measured, use the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you report or act on the number.\\n- For any PR-status request, use the **Babysit** playbook (`playbooks/babysit.md`).\\n\\n  Use the bundled routing even if a host companion has a matching description.\\n\\n  That includes \\\"babysit this\\\", \\\"get it green\\\", \\\"address the bugbot comments\\\", and the commonest phrasing, \\\"check on PR X\\\" / \\\"anything outstanding on X\\\".\\n\\n  Never triggered by merely opening a PR.\\n\\n  Declare its mode before polling.\\n\\n  The playbook's step 1 owns the request-to-mode mapping.\\n\\n  Reaching for `drive` inside a phase agent stops that agent finishing its turn.\\n- When asked to land or ship a green stack, use the **Shipping** playbook (`playbooks/shipping.md`). Green is not safe. Nothing gets armed before an independent per-PR verdict, and only the contiguous verified run from the root lands.\\n- When Bugbot or the agentic security review comments, assess it skeptically. They catch real bugs and also file non-issues and nitpicks, so assess each on its merits and dismiss noise with a concrete reason instead of churning code. Triage fix / dismiss / ask per `references/bugbot-triage.md`.\\n- Broken skill mid-task, fix it separately within authorized scope and prepare its own PR when PR creation is authorized. Continue independent work. Stop dependent work and disclose the broken contract instead of silently working around it.\\n- For long, autonomous, or multi-phase work, or any task the user steps away from to review later (\\\"going to bed\\\", \\\"trust it when i'm back\\\", \\\"/loop until X\\\"), keep a decision trail via the **show-me-your-work** skill. Commit it when stakes need an auditable record. Keep it local otherwise.\\n\\n## Principles\\n\\nRead the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies.\\n\\n**Core**\\n\\n- **Laziness Protocol** (**principle-laziness-protocol**). Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\n- **Foundational Thinking** (**principle-foundational-thinking**). Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.\\n- **Redesign from First Principles** (**principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.\\n- **Attack the Premise** (**principle-attack-the-premise**). Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.\\n- **Subtract Before You Add** (**principle-subtract-before-you-add**). Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.\\n- **Minimize Reader Load** (**principle-minimize-reader-load**). Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.\\n- **Outcome-Oriented Execution** (**principle-outcome-oriented-execution**). Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.\\n- **Experience First** (**principle-experience-first**). Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.\\n- **Exhaust the Design Space** (**principle-exhaust-the-design-space**). A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.\\n- **Build the Lever** (**principle-build-the-lever**). Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.\\n\\n**Architecture**\\n\\n- **Model the Domain** (**principle-model-the-domain**). Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.\\n- **Boundary Discipline** (**principle-boundary-discipline**). Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.\\n- **Type System Discipline** (**principle-type-system-discipline**). Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.\\n- **Make Operations Idempotent** (**principle-make-operations-idempotent**). Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.\\n- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs** (**principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.\\n- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State** (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.\\n\\n**Verification**\\n\\n- **Prove It Works** (**principle-prove-it-works**). After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or \\\"it compiles\\\".\\n- **Fix Root Causes** (**principle-fix-root-causes**). Debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it.\\n- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.\\n- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation** (**principle-test-behavior-not-implementation**). Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\\n- **Explain the Number** (**principle-explain-the-number**). Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.\\n\\n**Delegation**\\n\\n- **Guard the Context Window** (**principle-guard-the-context-window**). Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.\\n- **Never Block on the Human** (**principle-never-block-on-the-human**). Tempted to ask \\\"should I do X?\\\" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.\\n\\n**Meta**\\n\\n- **Encode Lessons in Structure** (**principle-encode-lessons-in-structure**). You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\n\\n## Autonomy\\n\\n**Just do it within authorization.** Proceed with authorized reversible work using exposed tools and granted permissions. Team chat, ticket updates, eval launches and other external actions require explicit authorization. Upstream autonomy language grants no permission. Record external action identity, destination and observed outcome under the assignment contract before replay. Unknown outcomes block replay.\\n\\n**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.\\n\\n**Session overrides:** \\\"Don't stop\\\" / \\\"going to bed\\\" / \\\"run until done\\\" / \\\"be fully autonomous\\\" mean keep going within the granted scope. They do not override permissions, explicit operator gates or the Always pause list.\\n\\n**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say \\\"this doesn't earn its place\\\" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.\\n\\n## Subagents\\n\\nUse the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) for any independent worker you spawn inside a playbook step, including code-writing delegates and ad-hoc helpers. /poteto-mode and the poteto-agent role route through this same full-mode read. Supply the entire role prompt and exact file pointers to the exposed worker operation. Generic routing without that prompt and read skips the style contract. Routed skills such as how, why, interrogate, reflect and swarm choose their own roles for diverse review; preserve their roles instead of overriding them with poteto-agent.\\n\\nDefaults for every worker assignment follow the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use independent background execution only when exposed and observed. Do not claim it from a role name or flag. Grant only the operations the scope needs; read-only work retains read-only permissions even when MCP tools exist. Use file pointers rather than inlined bulk context. Record requested and observed model and effort separately under [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md).\\n\\nCode delegates tier by difficulty. Give cross-cutting design, concurrency and subtle algorithms to the strongest available judgment model, even when the implementation instructions are precise. Trivial mechanical edits use an available fast code model. Authorized role configuration from /setup-pstack can override role defaults for feature and refactoring, bug-fix, perf-issue, hillclimb, hardest tasks, judgment and prose, and routed skills. Select only supported models and efforts from current tool documentation or observed enumeration. A missing role line keeps the portable inherit-parent default. A role line of inherit-parent or auto omits explicit model selection. Unsupported configured models or efforts require a disclosed supported fallback, or blocked if that exact choice is required. The source-host named defaults are not portable availability evidence. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified.\\n\\nWithout an exposed and authorized independent-worker operation, apply the same full-mode and leaf reads sequentially only within authorized scope. Label reduced capability. Sequential roles are not independent workers, independent review, background execution or model diversity. If the playbook requires independence, leave that gate blocked rather than silently waiving it.\\n\\nA worker forbidden to spawn owns its assigned diff directly and returns it to the lead for review separation, as Feature step 4 requires. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \\\"standing by\\\". This exception does not waive the lead's required independent review. Before accepting any result, match assignment identity, exact input revision, full current head SHA, existing artifacts and observed method evidence. Reject stale results and missing artifacts under the assignment contract. Bookkeeping labels cannot satisfy these checks.\\n\\nYou own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Treat agreement as supporting evidence only after checking independence, the observed models and the underlying artifacts.\\n\\n**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a \\\"done\\\" summary.\\n\\n## Throughput checkpoint\\n\\nFor nontrivial multi-step work, write these four todo items before fan-out, as required by Feature step 3. Keep an inapplicable dimension with n/a and a reason. Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries and return it with the evidence.\\n\\n- Blocking first steps. Gates run before fan-out.\\n- Independent workstreams. Disjoint files, services or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.\\n- Shared mutable state. Default to splitting the target using the separate-before-serializing-shared-state principle leaf. Serialize only for real invariants.\\n- Smallest safe decomposition. If one worker is best, name why.\\n\\nCode-coupled work goes to one owner with the checkpoint inline. That owner fans out after the blocking phase when authorized and supported. Parent-level fan-out is for independent artifacts. Assignment records and bookkeeping do not prove workers ran. Keep decision trails in an explicit owned local output path per show-me-your-work and its log helper contract. Missing helper setup or persistence stays visible; do not invent saved logs or cross-session continuity.\\n\\n## Integrated helper and delivery bindings\\n\\nRead the selected playbook's complete adapted helper and prompt contracts before dependent execution. The 23 bundled playbook routes below and the Bugbot rubric are local instructions. Historical task deferrals in those files are not proof of absence or permission to skip a present contract. Check the actual path. An absent required contract still blocks its dependent step.\\n\\n- Decision trails use [show-me-your-work](../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), its [template](../show-me-your-work/references/decision-log-template.tsv) and [log helper](../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh).\\n\\n  Invoke the helper through authorized execution with exactly `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`.\\n\\n  The nonempty logfile is an explicit owned local path.\\n\\n  Tabs, newlines and carriage returns are rejected before writes, and formula-leading cells are quoted.\\n\\n  Read back the trail and retain the skill's scoped transcript audit, cross-model review and Attention requirements.\\n\\n  Append-only logging proves neither unattended execution nor recovery.\\n- Multi-phase plans use [check-plan.mjs](scripts/check-plan.mjs) as `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/check-plan.mjs <plan.md>`.\\n\\n  It takes one positional path and reads without edits.\\n\\n  Exit 2 means usage or unreadable input, 1 means format problems, and 0 means structural success.\\n\\n  Keep capability declarations, live and perf evidence, independent review and exact-head receipts.\\n\\n  It checks pstack plans only.\\n\\n  It never validates another controller's plan, implementation or host behavior.\\n- Orchestrate <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/orch/orch.ts --store <owned-store>` or explicit `ORCH_STORE` outside the package tree.\\n\\n  Use full JSON for standing orders and rows.\\n\\n  Preserve `inbox drain --peek --json` and actual drain receipts with durable readback before classification. `ledger check <pr> <full-head-sha>` returns NOT-VERIFIED and exit 2 for a missing key.\\n\\n  Usage or runtime errors exit 1.\\n\\n  Ledger rows replace the same key without enforcing verifier precedence.\\n\\n  The caller owns precedence, append-only attempt history, exact SHA syntax, artifact inspection, terminal states, permissions and current-head filtering.\\n\\n  The helper never spawns, waits or wakes workers.\\n\\n  Stale locks require ownership review, and `--force` requires read-only [watcher](scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) through their complete playbooks.\\n\\n  From the package root bind `bun --no-install skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr` with explicit `--owner`, `--repo`, PR selection, `--head <number=full-40-character-head>` for every watched member, `--max-polls <remaining-count>` and `--timeout <remaining-seconds>`.\\n\\n  Freeze queued order with `--queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom-to-top-list>`.\\n\\n  Connected mode uses `--stack`, mutually exclusive with queued mode. `check` adds `--status-only`.\\n\\n  Inspect NDJSON schemaVersion 1 State the done predicate and the artifact or report the swarm must return.\\n2. Choose the shape. Partition into slices, race N workers on identical briefs, or mix both. For a race or mixed shape, declare `first pass`, `rank all`, or `best-of` before spawning.\\n3. Set N from the user or derive it from the shape. N is total workers, not the host concurrency limit.\\n4. Select the swarm worker model through current exposed model capabilities and the user's selection. Create immutable assignments and append-only attempt events under the assignment contract. Prefer cloud/background execution when supported and authorized. Use local execution only when the worker needs something on the user's computer. If the host cannot provide the requested environment, disclose the limit before an authorized alternative. A non-default pushed branch requires an exposed base-branch binding and exact revision verification; never infer checkout from a branch label.\\n\\nEvery brief stands alone. Include the goal, scope, exact slice or race arm, how to verify, and what to report. Reports use `PASS`, `ISSUES`, or `BLOCKED` with evidence and links to existing artifacts. A worker that can prove a defect reports `ISSUES` and lists every issue it can prove, not only the first. Authorized sequential work is reduced capability. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\n\\n### Communication artifacts\\n\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\"I hope this helps!\\\", \\\"Let me know if...\\\", \\\"Of course!\\\", \\\"Certainly!\\\", \\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\" Remove.\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\"Great question! You're absolutely right!\\\" Respond directly.\\n\\n### Filler\\n\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\"In order to\\\" becomes \\\"To\\\". \\\"Due to the fact that\\\" becomes \\\"Because\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" gets deleted.\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\" becomes \\\"may\\\".\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\"The future looks bright.\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\n\\n### Jargon\\n\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\"API surface\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\"Substrate\\\" becomes \\\"base\\\". \\\"Wedge in\\\" becomes \\\"add\\\". \\\"Vector\\\" becomes \\\"way\\\" or \\\"method\\\". \\\"Gold-plating\\\" becomes \\\"more than the job needs\\\". \\\"Ratchet\\\" becomes the mechanism's real name or \\\"a limit that only tightens\\\". \\\"Evacuate\\\" becomes \\\"move out\\\". \\\"Endgame\\\" becomes \\\"the last phase\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\n\\n### Plain speech\\n\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\"the database stays close at hand\\\", \\\"SQL you can read\\\", \\\"types that follow your schema\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\", \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\" and name the actor: \\\"queries are validated\\\" becomes \\\"the compiler validates queries\\\", \\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\" becomes \\\"the loader parses the file\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\"runs quickly\\\" becomes \\\"is fast\\\" or the number. \\\"significantly improves\\\" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.\\n31. **Prefer the plain word.** \\\"utilize\\\" becomes \\\"use\\\", \\\"leverage\\\" becomes \\\"use\\\", \\\"facilitate\\\" becomes \\\"help\\\", \\\"numerous\\\" becomes \\\"many\\\", \\\"in the event that\\\" becomes \\\"if\\\". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.\\n32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms (\\\"wire it or delete it\\\"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code (\\\"the plan holds it\\\"), figurative verbs (\\\"rides along\\\", \\\"stands on\\\"), stock framing phrases. \\\"A dial worth turning\\\" becomes \\\"a parameter worth varying\\\". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.\\n33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. \\\"Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write\\\" becomes \\\"The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.\\\" Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.\\n\\nFILE skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: technical-writing\\ndescription: \\\"Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Technical writing\\n\\nThe goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.\\n\\nThree rules sit above the layers:\\n\\n- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. \\\"In order to\\\" is \\\"to\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" is nothing.\\n- **Use the short, everyday word.** \\\"Use\\\", not \\\"utilize\\\". \\\"Help\\\", not \\\"facilitate\\\". \\\"Do\\\", not \\\"perform\\\". A long word has to buy its length with precision.\\n- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.\\n\\nThe codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.\\n\\nDon't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: \\\"move\\\", \\\"delete\\\", \\\"a budget that only decreases\\\", not \\\"evacuate\\\", \\\"ratchet\\\", or \\\"endgame\\\". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.\\n\\n## Vary the rhythm\\n\\nThe layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.\\n\\n- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.\\n- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.\\n- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.\\n- Be specific over sterile. Not \\\"schema changes can cause issues\\\" but \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\".\\n\\n## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)\\n\\nOne document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?\\n\\n- Action + learning: **tutorial**.\\n- Action + work: **how-to**.\\n- Understanding + work: **reference**.\\n- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.\\n\\nUse the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.\\n\\n**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will \\\"learn\\\". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as \\\"we\\\", in commands: \\\"First, do x. Now, do y.\\\"\\n\\n**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: \\\"If you want x, do y.\\\" Name the guide by the task: \\\"How to calibrate the radar array\\\", not \\\"Radar array calibration\\\".\\n\\n**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.\\n\\n**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit \\\"About...\\\" in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.\\n\\nDon't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.\\n\\n## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)\\n\\n- Talk to the reader as \\\"you\\\", in the present tense. \\\"Will\\\" only for things that genuinely happen later.\\n- Say who does what: \\\"the compiler checks\\\", not \\\"is checked\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.\\n- Write instructions as commands: \\\"Click Submit.\\\" State facts plainly. Never \\\"should be done\\\".\\n- Put the condition before the instruction: \\\"To delete the document, click Delete.\\\" The reader skips what does not apply.\\n- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.\\n- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no \\\"please\\\" in instructions, and never \\\"simply\\\", \\\"easy\\\", or \\\"quickly\\\" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.\\n- Don't pre-announce (\\\"we will soon support...\\\") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.\\n- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never \\\"click here\\\". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.\\n- Headings carry the point, not just the topic (\\\"Pick the mode first\\\", not \\\"Modes\\\"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase (\\\"Create an instance\\\"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.\\n- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.\\n- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop \\\"etc.\\\" and say up front that a list is partial.\\n\\n## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)\\n\\n- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.\\n- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.\\n- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: \\\"If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur.\\\"\\n- Keep \\\"the\\\" and \\\"a\\\": \\\"Remove backup file\\\" reads two ways. \\\"Remove the backup file\\\" reads one.\\n- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If \\\"check\\\" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.\\n- Pick one word per action and stick to it: \\\"start\\\", not \\\"start\\\" here and \\\"initiate\\\" there.\\n- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: \\\"Install the component\\\", not \\\"the component must be installed\\\".\\n- Avoid \\\"-ing\\\" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.\\n\\n## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)\\n\\n- Keep words like \\\"only\\\" and \\\"not\\\" next to the word they change: \\\"only fails on growth\\\" and \\\"fails only on growth\\\" say different things.\\n- Break up long noun strings: \\\"the proto import budget check script\\\" becomes \\\"the script that checks the proto-import budget\\\".\\n- Make every \\\"it\\\", \\\"they\\\", and \\\"this\\\" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use \\\"this\\\" or \\\"which\\\" to point at a whole clause.\\n- Don't drop verbs: \\\"Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime\\\" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.\\n- Keep the small words that show structure. \\\"Ensure that the switch is off\\\" keeps \\\"that\\\" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.\\n- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: \\\"the client and the host\\\", not \\\"the client and host\\\", when they are two things.\\n- Say which parts \\\"and\\\" or \\\"or\\\" joins when a sentence can group two ways. \\\"Both...and\\\", \\\"either...or\\\", and \\\"if...then\\\" are free disambiguators.\\n- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.\\n- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with \\\"(s)\\\".\\n- No slashes: write \\\"a, b, or both\\\" instead of \\\"a/b\\\" or \\\"and/or\\\".\\n- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says \\\"the gate\\\", \\\"the ratchet\\\", and \\\"the budget check\\\" for one thing teaches three things. Rewording an unchanged sentence between edits costs the same way. Don't churn what didn't change.\\n- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.\\n\\n## Voice and repo specifics\\n\\n- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.\\n- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.\\n- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.\\n- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.\\n\\n## Worked example\\n\\nBefore:\\n\\n> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.\\n\\nAfter:\\n\\n> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.\\n\\n## Access and permissions\\n\\nUse the current session capabilities in `../../references/host-capabilities.md` to read documents and verify authorized edits. Supplied text is enough for a rewrite in the conversation. If document writes are unavailable or denied, return the proposed text and state that it was not saved. If the document cannot be read and no text was supplied, report the missing input. Do not invent its content. Read `../unslop/SKILL.md` before applying it. If that dependency is unavailable, report the gap and label the review partial. Preserve `disable-model-invocation` as source metadata; host enforcement needs observed evidence. These limits also apply to PR descriptions and commit messages. Sending, publishing, or creating external changes requires explicit authorization.\\n\\nFILE skills/principle-make-operations-idempotent/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: principle-make-operations-idempotent\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Make Operations Idempotent\\n\\nDesign operations so they converge to the correct state regardless of how many times they run or where they start from. Every state-mutating operation should answer: \\\"What happens if this runs twice? What happens if the previous run crashed halfway?\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Commands, lifecycle operations, and processing loops run where crashes, restarts, and retries are normal. If partial state changes the next run's outcome, every restart becomes a debugging session.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- Convergent startup: scan for existing state, clean stale artifacts, adopt live sessions\\n- Content-based cleanup: compare by content equivalence, not creation order\\n- Self-healing locks: use PID-based stale lock detection\\n- Idempotent scheduling: failed work respawns cleanly, fresh input regenerated after each cycle\\n\\n**The test:**\\n1. What happens if this runs twice in a row?\\n2. What happens if the previous run crashed at every possible point?\\n3. Does re-execution converge to the same end state?\\n\\nIf any answer is \\\"it depends on what state was left behind,\\\" the operation needs a reconciliation step.\\n\\n## Capability and recovery boundaries\\n\\nUse [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to establish the tools and permissions available for inspection, execution and durable state. Apply the [assignment and integration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md) when recovery involves worker attempts or interrupted external actions.\\n\\nBefore replaying an external action, record explicit authorization, a stable action identity, its destination and the last observed outcome. Inspect the prior action and destination state after interruption. Recognize completed actions without repeating their side effects. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to that destination. An unknown outcome blocks replay. Local convergence alone does not establish external replay safety.\\n\\nIf inspection, writes, execution or persistence are unavailable, state the missing capability and provide an authorized reduced recovery design where useful. Identify checks and actions not performed; do not claim successful recovery, durable continuity or unattended execution from a design alone. Preserve the invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\n\\nFILE skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: principle-build-the-lever\\ndescription: \\\"Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n# Build the Lever\\n\\nWhen the work isn't trivial, build the tool that does it instead of doing it by hand.\\n\\n**Why:** Two payoffs. Throughput: a codemod, generator, or script does the work the same way every time and reruns for free. Confidence: the tool is one artifact a reviewer can read and rerun to check the work. Hand-done changes can only be re-verified by redoing them. A deterministic script turns \\\"trust me\\\" into \\\"run this\\\".\\n\\n**Pattern:** Default to building the lever. Skip it only when the task is trivial, a couple of obvious edits you can see at a glance.\\n\\n- Do the first unit by hand to learn the recipe, then build the tool. Prove it by rerunning it on that unit and diffing against your hand-done version. Make the lever safe to rerun.\\n- Codemod or script for edits, generator for repetitive files, a dump-to-sqlite query for analysis, a rerunnable check for verification.\\n- A deterministic lever beats fan-out. If the tool can process every unit in one pass, run it yourself. Don't fan out delegates to hand-apply what a script can do.\\n- When you fan work out to subagents, write the lever as a skill they all read: the recipe, the verification contract, and the do-not-touch fences in one artifact. Keep it outside the delegates' write scope so they can't quietly edit the contract.\\n- Applying this principle produces a file. If you cited it and there is no codemod, script, generator, or delegate skill in the diff, you didn't apply it.\\n- Commit the lever when the work outlives the session.\\n\\n**Balance:** The bar is triviality, not repetition. A one-off still earns a lever when the lever is what makes the work checkable. Per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md), build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework.\\n\\nDistinct from [Encode Lessons in Structure](../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md), which makes a recurring instruction a durable guardrail. This is throughput and reviewability on the work in front of you. For scripting the verification itself, see [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\n## Host capability and permission boundaries\\n\\nUse the [host capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to discover file reads, authorized writes, execution and persistence. A proposed tool is not a saved artifact. A saved artifact is not executed proof. Report the commands, exit status and comparisons you observed; if execution is denied or unavailable, state that proof is blocked and provide the proposed rerun and diff procedure as reduced capability. If source reads are unavailable, do not claim a verified recipe.\\n\\nDelegation requires user authorization and exposed independent-worker operations under the [orchestration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Keep the shared recipe outside worker write scopes. Sequential work is reduced capability and never proves independent workers. Preserve the [active workflow owner](../../references/workflow-ownership.md).\\n\\nRetaining the lever beyond the session does not grant commit permission. Commit only when authorized. Do not install dependencies, publish or perform external writes as incidental steps. Preserve `disable-model-invocation: true` metadata without assuming the host enforces it.\\n\\n\"\n    }\n  },\n  {\n    \"tool\": \"exec_command\",\n    \"args\": {\n      \"cmd\": \"git ls-tree -r show-me-your-work\\ndescription: \\\"Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. candidate\\n- Skip when: The PR description, screenshots, design review, or nearby code makes the visual change explicit, and the Bugbot comment is only restating that a shared visual default changed.\\n- Do not skip when: The comment points to accessibility, focus visibility, keyboard navigation, color contrast, or a component API contract that the PR did not intentionally change.\\n- stack-local usage Bugbot cannot see\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: Bugbot flags an export, component, helper, or file as unused, and the active forge's PR list and diffs, upper-stack diffs, or PR context show it is used by a later PR in the stack.\\n- Do not skip when: The current PR is not part of a stack, the symbol is public API, or the supposed upstack use cannot be verified.\\n- Example signal: \\\"Exported component is never used\\\" with a human reply like \\\"used upstack\\\".\\n\\n### Temporary duplication during parallel implementation\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The PR intentionally duplicates a small amount of code to keep a new path parallel to an old path that is being deleted, replaced, or proven out.\\n- Do not skip when: The duplicated code changes security, billing, data access, API behavior, or a long-lived shared abstraction would clearly reduce risk.\\n- Example signal: \\\"Significant duplication\\\" or \\\"duplicated validation logic\\\" where the owner explains the old path will be deleted or the duplicate logic is intentionally local.\\n\\n### Existing framework or component invariant covers the warning\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The concern is already guaranteed by a shared component, framework contract, type invariant, or single source of truth visible in the current diff or nearby code.\\n- Do not skip when: The invariant is assumed but not enforced, depends on timing, or crosses async/state boundaries where values can diverge.\\n- Example signal: Comments about missing max-height on an inner popover when the shared popover enforces viewport bounds, or nullable values where the local checked value and passed value share the same source.\\n\\n### regression.\\n- Example signal: \\\"I'll worry about that later\\\" or \\\"we'll delete this eventually\\\".\\n\\n### Self-withdrawn or explicit false-positive rule comments\\n\\n- Confidence: recurring\\n- Skip when: The comment body or a later Bugbot reply explicitly says the finding is withdrawn, compliant, or a false positive, and the agent can verify the relevant rule locally.\\n- Do not skip when: The only evidence is a human saying \\\"false positive\\\" on a high-risk issue without explanation.\\n- Example signal: A file-naming rule comment whose body says the file is already compliant.\\n\\n## Ask by default\\n\\nDo not auto-skip these categories, even if a previous PR dismissed something similar:\\n\\n- Security, privacy, auth, billing, data retention, training-data, and
